source_class: wire observation and public Go API/artifact observation
tool: Go 1.27.3 linux/amd64 public conformance.PlayClient scripted probes; Temurin JDK 25.0.5+8 official server oracles

oracle_configuration.operators: source and secondary peer have level 4 offline UUID entries

observed_commands.note: The success echo is nested in chat.type.admin. Only successful level-4 invocations were newly measured; no new permission-denial or invalid-argument claim is made.

compact_go_api_pin.api: public server.New and Server.SaveWorld, invoked outside simulation ownership
compact_go_api_pin.format: existing canonical version-2 JSON overrides; overworld WorldPath, then .the_nether and .the_end
observations: Successful SaveWorld return precedes reading and copying all three complete artifacts, before closing any client or stopping the original runtime.

Copied canonical identities include explicit air replacing generated overworld grass, overworld oak_log[axis=x], the_nether oak_log[axis=z], and the_end stone. The same coordinates in different dimensions retain their distinct identities.

A later distinct source generation is saved; a fresh runtime starts from the earlier copied files. Both 775/776 clients independently decode the initial chunks, verify explicit air at the exact cell and query the complete expected descriptors through execute-if-block commands.
scope_limits: WorldPath compact block overrides only; no native WorldDir, player, inventory, chest or block-entity save guarantee is added.

The probe does not claim overlap with physical I/O, bounded latency, crash consistency across dimensions, fsync or power-loss durability. Deterministic blocked-writer tests separately establish owner responsiveness and ordering.
The vanilla command checks exercise the unchanged synchronous native save path and do not establish compact Go persistence semantics.
